properties.name: reflow2 can say which of its own skills and tools a session reached for — recorded automatically, reported without judgement
properties.statement:
reflow2 RECORDS which of its own skills were fetched and which tools were called in a session, automatically and without the agent's cooperation, and reports it as a fact rather than a verdict.

WHY IT IS FIRST, AND THIS IS THE WHOLE ARGUMENT FOR THE ORDERING: `req:a-discipline-is-delivered-at-the-tool-not-in-a-catalogue` proposes to raise a rate that HAS NEVER BEEN OBSERVED. `dec:bl-155` measured TOOL calls — 6,095 across 46 retained transcripts, 40 of 132 tools never called — and there has never been an equivalent for `get_skill`, which is server-side and trivially countable. **Ship the hints first and there is no way to tell whether anything changed; the project would be optimising a number it cannot see.** So this is not the interesting work and it goes first anyway.

AUTOMATIC, NOT A TOOL — and the reason is self-defeat rather than convenience. A tool must be CALLED, and the population most worth measuring is precisely the one least likely to call it: an agent that forgets `revise-design` forgets `log_usage` too. The measurement would be biased toward the sessions that need no measuring. Every MCP call already passes through the server, so the server records without being asked. Anthony reached this himself while proposing it (\"maybe a tool is not the right option\").

REPORTS, DOES NOT DIAGNOSE — his constraint, and already this project's doctrine: `dec:report-dont-judge` holds that the confirmation ledger reports claim history and never judges a claim. Same shape one domain over.

⚠️ WHAT IT CAN AND CANNOT MEASURE, stated up front because reporting the wrong one would be the exact false confidence the loop exists to prevent: **it measures FETCHES, NOT COMPLIANCE.** A skill can be followed correctly from memory without ever being fetched — this session followed revise-design's snapshot-first step without loading it — and a skill can be fetched and ignored. BL-155's own caveat travels: absence is WEAK evidence, and `set_project_mode` appeared as text in ten transcripts with zero recorded calls despite having been used. A rising fetch count is evidence that the routing changed, never evidence that the discipline held.

WHERE THE LOG LIVES is deliberately NOT settled here — `dec:how-should-reflow2-log-its-own-usage` holds that question, with the recommendation (beside the store, not in the graph) and its precedent (the shared-mode rendezvous and log already sit beside the store rather than inside it).

SOURCE: Anthony, 2026-08-09 — \"something that automatically logs usage and issues (doesn't diagnose, just logs)\".
